title: timeparse ignores a leading minus sign
body:
`timeparse` in `pytimeparse/timeparse.py` documents signed expressions,
but the sign has no effect:

```python
>>> timeparse("- 1 minute")
60     # expected -60
>>> timeparse("-1:24")
84     # expected -84
```

Expected: a leading "-" (optionally followed by spaces) negates the
result for every supported format, and a leading "+" keeps it
positive (`timeparse("+ 1 minute") == 60`).
provenance: upstream code at a pinned commit with an injected regression; the oracle is the unmodified upstream file

source.modifications: reformatted with black (layout and quote style only) to pass the repository formatting check; snapshot adds the injected defect, visible tests and empty package markers

defect: The sign is read from a misspelled group name, so it is always positive.
